name: Baghdad
summary: Founded in 762 by the caliph al-Mansur as a perfectly round 'City of Peace', Baghdad became the capital of the Abbasid caliphate and, for a time, the largest and most learned city on Earth — the Baghdad of Harun al-Rashid, the House of Wisdom and the Thousand and One Nights. The Mongols ended that golden age in 1258. Ottoman for centuries, it became the capital of Iraq in 1921 and the stage, within living memory, for revolution, dictatorship and war. It still stands on the Tigris that made it.

figures.label: Population
figures.note: Greater Baghdad; the largest city in Iraq.

figures.label: Founded
figures.note: By the Abbasid caliph al-Mansur as the round “City of Peace.”

figures.label: Setting
figures.note: In the Mesopotamian plain of central Iraq.

figures.label: Golden Age
figures.note: The world’s largest city and its greatest centre of learning.

figures.label: Known for
figures.note: And the tales of the Thousand and One Nights.

events.title: Al-Mansur founds Baghdad
events.body: The Abbasid caliph al-Mansur builds the round “City of Peace” on the Tigris.

events.title: Harun al-Rashid
events.body: Under Harun al-Rashid, Baghdad becomes the fabled city of the Thousand and One Nights.

events.title: The House of Wisdom
events.body: Caliph al-Ma’mun makes Baghdad the world’s centre of learning and translation.

events.title: The court moves to Samarra
events.body: The caliphs briefly shift the capital upriver to Samarra.

events.title: The caliphs return
events.body: Baghdad resumes as the Abbasid capital and remains the largest city in the world.

events.title: The Buyids take power
events.body: Persian Buyid emirs seize real power, keeping the caliph as a figurehead.

events.title: The Seljuk Turks
events.body: Seljuk sultans enter Baghdad and rule in the caliph’s name.

events.title: The Mustansiriya
events.body: One of the world’s first true universities is founded in Baghdad.

events.title: The Mongol sack
events.body: Hulagu Khan destroys Baghdad and kills the last Abbasid caliph — the end of the golden age.

events.title: Timur’s massacre
events.body: Timur sacks Baghdad and, by report, builds towers from the skulls of the dead.

events.title: The Ottomans
events.body: Süleyman the Magnificent takes Baghdad for the Ottoman Empire.

events.title: A Safavid interlude
events.body: Persia’s Safavids seize Baghdad before the Ottomans retake it.

events.title: Ottoman reconquest
events.body: Murad IV storms Baghdad; it stays Ottoman for nearly three centuries.

events.title: Midhat Pasha reforms
events.body: A reforming governor begins to modernise the city.

events.title: The British take Baghdad
events.body: British forces capture Baghdad from the Ottomans in the First World War.

events.title: Capital of Iraq
events.body: Baghdad becomes the capital of the new Kingdom of Iraq under King Faisal I.

events.title: Independence
events.body: Iraq gains independence, with Baghdad as its capital.

events.title: The monarchy falls
events.body: A revolution overthrows the monarchy and Iraq becomes a republic.

events.title: The Ba’ath seize power
events.body: A coup brings the Ba’ath Party — and eventually Saddam Hussein — to power.

events.title: Saddam takes control
events.body: Saddam Hussein becomes president, ruling Iraq from Baghdad.

events.title: The Gulf War
events.body: US-led bombing strikes Baghdad after Iraq’s invasion of Kuwait.

events.title: The US invasion
events.body: American forces take Baghdad and Saddam’s statue is toppled.

events.title: Sectarian war
events.body: Baghdad is torn by sectarian violence at the height of the insurgency.

places.name: The Round City
places.note: Al-Mansur’s perfectly circular “City of Peace,” long since vanished.

places.name: Mustansiriya
places.note: One of the oldest surviving universities in the world.

places.name: The Tigris
places.note: The river along which Baghdad was built and burned.

places.name: Tahrir Square
places.note: The civic square of the modern city.

caveats: This timeline is compiled from general reference works — listed under Sources — rather than an event-by-event archive of primary documents, as the Mumbai timeline is. Treat it as a reliable outline, not a citation of record.
Dates for the earliest, legendary events are traditional rather than documented.

dynasties.note: Dynasties and houses that shaped Baghdad.

list.name: The Abbasid caliphs
list.summary: The dynasty that built Baghdad and made it the heart of an Islamic golden age, until the Mongols killed the last caliph.

list.name: The Barmakids
list.legacy: The learned court of Harun al-Rashid
list.summary: A family of viziers who ran the empire and patronised its learning under Harun al-Rashid.

list.name: The Hashemites
list.summary: The dynasty installed by Britain to rule the new Iraqi state from Baghdad.
